Md. Abdus Salam and others
Vs.
Md. Abul Hasem Sarder and others
full_judgment: 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and submits that the learned appellate court below in deciding the fate of the appeal and in passing the impugned judgment and decree committed no illegality or irregularity. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate further submits that the pattern settlement as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs is not proved as genuine and it was not valid inasmuch as it was not completed by giving rent or salami in favour of the landlord. There is no document showing that the landlord accepted rent or salami from the settlement holder and as such the settlement was not completed and thus it does not confer any right, title, interest in favour of anybody. The learned Advocate further submits that under section 57 of the Mohamadan Law there is a concept of joint family which has been reflected within the decision given by this court in a case law reported in 14 BLD253 and their lordships in the case of Daliluddin Sheikh and others -vs.- Alek Sheikh alias Adul Malek Sheikh and others reported in 3XP(AD)7 held that there is no presumption of joint family in the Muslim Law but it appears that, sometimes after the death of father, all the members of that family use to reside and are in one mess and common income and in that position the property purchased in the name of one member of said family can be considered as property purchased for all. The learned Advocate also submits that earlier the plaintiffs in respect of self-same property and same relief instituted a Title Suit being No. 108 of 1999 which has been marked as Exhibit-"Jha". The suit was between the same parties. That suit was dismissed and two years after that; the present suit is filed by the plaintiffs for the same relief in respect of the same property with an additional prayer for partition and thereby this suit is not maintainable and barred by law. In this context; the learned Advocate referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 182 BLD (AD)54. The learned Advocate submits that admittedly the plaintiff's predecessor Madar Sarder was the elder brother and he had another brother Nur Mohammad by name. From Exhibit-"Gha" it appears that Mader Sardar personally by his presence prepared the S.A. record and subsequent to that; the R.S. record was prepared in the names of two brothers and their mother which is a document on record showing the bonafide of the defendants. It is in evidence that Madar Sarder alone never acquired the land and the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiffs are contradictory with one another and they have hopelessly failed to prove the alleged title and possession over the suit land. By virtue of Exhibit-4 the kabla deed it appears that the two brothers jointly sold out some properties and the case of the defendants is such that in the year 1990 the two sons of Madar Sander plaintiffs No. 1 and 2 purchased some land of the suit holding from Abdul Khaleque and from this document as well as form the examination-in-chief of the plaintiff's witness no.2 it is proved that the plaintiffs are possessing a particular portion of land as decided by the lower appellate court. In this context; the learned appellate court rightly held that in that portion of land the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief since their purchase is not challenged or disproved by any cogent evidence. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the defendants in the year 1984 mutated their names in respect of the suit land and paying rent regularly and the kabla deeds of the defendants dated 10.06.1969 and 02.12.1969 which has been marked as Exhibits-'Gha' and Uma are not challenged by the plaintiffs and as such it is admitted that these kabla deeds were executed by their predecessor Madar Sarder in respect of the suit holding. The learned appellate court in his observation and findings after proper assessment of evidence in its true perspective decided the matter-in-issue rightly in favour of the defendant No. 5 and in passing the impugned judgment and decree there is no infirmity or illegality done for which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with.
